docs.title: Welcome to SwiftBox Help Center
docs.text:
SwiftBox provides reliable parcel delivery services for businesses and individuals. Use this help center to create your first order, track shipments, manage billing, and integrate SwiftBox with your own systems.

Get Started

docs.title: 🚀 Fast Nationwide Delivery
docs.text: Ship parcels to any supported destination with predictable delivery windows. Our distribution network is designed to move shipments quickly and keep recipients informed.

docs.title: 📍 Real-Time Tracking
docs.text: Track each shipment with detailed status updates, estimated delivery times, and location history. For automated updates, configure webhook notifications.

docs.title: 🔒 Secure Handling
docs.text:
SwiftBox follows documented handling procedures from pickup through delivery. Each order is associated with a tracking number so you can monitor the shipment lifecycle from the dashboard or API.

Note

New to SwiftBox? Start with the Getting Started guide to create an account and place your first order.

docs.title: Quick Navigation
docs.text:
• Getting Started - Set up your account and place your first order.
  • Order Tracking - Track shipments and configure webhook notifications.
  • Pricing & Billing - Compare pricing tiers, payment methods, taxes, and invoices.
  • Partner API - Integrate SwiftBox order and tracking workflows into your application.

Tip

Use the Partner API to automate order creation, retrieve tracking details, and manage webhook subscriptions.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
Need help with an order, invoice, or API integration? Email support@swiftbox.com and include your order ID or tracking number when available.

For common account, payment, and plan questions, see the Pricing & Billing FAQ.

docs.text:

docs.title: Partner API
docs.text:
The SwiftBox Partner API provides programmatic access to delivery services, including order creation, tracking, webhook management, and account workflows. Build custom integrations that automate your shipping operations.

Note

The current API version is v1. Breaking changes will be announced with a migration guide before a new version becomes required.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All API requests require authentication with an API key. Include your key in the X-API-Key header with each request.

Warning

Never expose your API key in client-side code or public repositories. Rotate keys immediately if they are compromised.

docs.title: Obtaining Your API Key
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Settings > API Keys in your dashboard.
  2. Click Generate New Key.
  3. Copy the key and store it securely.
  4. Keys are displayed only once. Save them immediately.

Note

Business and Enterprise plans support multiple API keys with granular permissions for different applications or environments.

docs.title: Authentication Failure Example
docs.text:
Requests with a missing or invalid API key return 401 Unauthorized.

curl -i -X GET https://api.swiftbox.com/api/v1/orders/SBX-789456123 \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"

{
  "error": {
    "code": "unauthorized",
    "message": "A valid API key is required.",
    "request_id": "req_01HZX7A4Q7Y3Z"
  }
}

docs.title: API Endpoints
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description POST /api/v1/orders Create a new delivery order. GET /api/v1/orders/{order_id} Retrieve order details. PATCH /api/v1/orders/{order_id} Update order details. DELETE /api/v1/orders/{order_id} Cancel an order. GET /api/v1/orders/{order_id}/tracking Get real-time tracking status. GET /api/v1/webhooks List configured webhooks. POST /api/v1/webhooks Register a new webhook. DELETE /api/v1/webhooks/{webhook_id} Remove a webhook.

docs.title: Create an Order
docs.text:
Creates a new delivery order and returns the assigned order ID and tracking number.

cURL

curl -i -X POST https://api.swiftbox.com/api/v1/orders \
  -H "X-API-Key: your_api_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "recipient": {
      "name": "Jane Smith",
      "address": "123 Main St",
      "city": "San Francisco",
      "state": "CA",
      "zip": "94102",
      "country": "US",
      "phone": "+14155551234"
    },
    "package": {
      "weight": 2.5,
      "dimensions": {
        "length": 12,
        "width": 8,
        "height": 4
      }
    },
    "service_level": "express"
  }'

Python

import requests

url = "https://api.swiftbox.com/api/v1/orders"
headers = {
    "X-API-Key": "your_api_key_here",
    "Content-Type": "application/json",
}
payload = {
    "recipient": {
        "name": "Jane Smith",
        "address": "123 Main St",
        "city": "San Francisco",
        "state": "CA",
        "zip": "94102",
        "country": "US",
        "phone": "+14155551234",
    },
    "package": {
        "weight": 2.5,
        "dimensions": {
            "length": 12,
            "width": 8,
            "height": 4,
        },
    },
    "service_level": "express",
}

try:
    response = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=10)
    response.raise_for_status()
except requests.HTTPError as exc:
    print(f"SwiftBox API error: {exc.response.status_code} {exc.response.text}")
    raise
except requests.RequestException as exc:
    print(f"Network error calling SwiftBox: {exc}")
    raise

order = response.json()
print(f"Order created: {order['order_id']}")

Example response

{
  "order_id": "SBX-789456123",
  "tracking_number": "1Z999AA10123456784",
  "status": "PENDING_PICKUP",
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:00:00Z"
}

  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

      "phone": "+14155559876"
    },
    "delivery_instructions": "Leave with front desk."

docs.title: Cancel an Order
docs.text:
Use DELETE to cancel an order before it is picked up.

curl -i -X DELETE https://api.swiftbox.com/api/v1/orders/SBX-789456123 \
  -H "X-API-Key: your_api_key_here"

  "cancelled_at": "2025-01-15T10:20:00Z"
}

docs.title: List Webhooks
docs.text:
Use limit and offset to paginate webhook subscriptions. The default limit is 10; the maximum limit is 100.

curl -i -X GET "https://api.swiftbox.com/api/v1/webhooks?limit=10&offset=0" \
  -H "X-API-Key: your_api_key_here"

{
  "data": [
    {
      "webhook_id": "wh_01HZX6VC8R9K",
      "url": "https://example.com/webhooks/swiftbox",
      "events": ["order.created", "order.status_updated"],
      "active": true,
      "created_at": "2025-01-10T09:00:00Z"
    }
  ],
  "pagination": {
    "limit": 10,
    "offset": 0,
    "total": 1,
    "next": null
  }
}

docs.title: Register a Webhook
docs.text:
Register a webhook endpoint and secret. SwiftBox uses the secret to sign webhook requests.

curl -i -X POST https://api.swiftbox.com/api/v1/webhooks \
  -H "X-API-Key: your_api_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "url": "https://example.com/webhooks/swiftbox",
    "events": [
      "order.created",
      "order.status_updated",
      "order.cancelled"
    ],
    "secret": "replace_with_a_strong_random_secret"
  }'

{
  "webhook_id": "wh_01HZX6VC8R9K",
  "url": "https://example.com/webhooks/swiftbox",
  "events": [
    "order.created",
    "order.status_updated",
    "order.cancelled"
  ],
  "active": true,
  "created_at": "2025-01-15T10:25:00Z"
}

See Webhook Security for HMAC verification guidance.

curl -i -X DELETE https://api.swiftbox.com/api/v1/webhooks/wh_01HZX6VC8R9K \

{
  "webhook_id": "wh_01HZX6VC8R9K",

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text:
Errors use a consistent JSON envelope.

HTTP Status Code Meaning 400 bad_request The request body, query parameter, or path parameter is invalid. 401 unauthorized The API key is missing, invalid, or expired. 403 forbidden The API key does not have permission for the requested resource. 404 not_found The requested order, shipment, or webhook was not found. 429 rate_limited The account exceeded the allowed request rate. 500 internal_error SwiftBox could not process the request due to an internal error.

docs.title: Rate Limits
docs.text:
API requests are rate-limited to ensure fair usage:

  • Starter: 100 requests per minute
  • Business: 1,000 requests per minute
  • Enterprise: 10,000 requests per minute

Rate limit headers are included in every API response:

  • X-RateLimit-Limit: Maximum requests allowed in the current window.
  • X-RateLimit-Remaining: Requests remaining in the current window.
  • X-RateLimit-Reset: Unix timestamp when the current window resets.
  • Retry-After: Seconds to wait before retrying, included with 429 responses.

Example 429 Too Many Requests response:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 100
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1736953200
Retry-After: 30

{
  "error": {
    "code": "rate_limited",
    "message": "Rate limit exceeded. Retry after 30 seconds.",
    "request_id": "req_01HZX7A4Q7Y3E"
  }
}

Tip

Implement exponential backoff when receiving 429 Too Many Requests responses, and use the Retry-After header when it is present.

docs.title: Pricing & Billing
docs.text: SwiftBox offers flexible pricing plans for businesses of all sizes. Choose the tier that matches your shipping volume, integration needs, and support requirements.

docs.title: Pricing Tiers
docs.text:
Feature Starter Business Enterprise Monthly shipments Up to 50 51-500 500+ Standard delivery ✓ ✓ ✓ Express delivery ✓ ✓ ✓ Same-day delivery ✗ ✓ ✓ API access Basic Full Full + Custom Webhook notifications 1,000/month 50,000/month Unlimited Dedicated support Email Email & Phone 24/7 Priority Custom integrations ✗ ✗ ✓ Monthly cost $29 $149 Custom

Note

All plans include real-time tracking, insurance up to $100 per shipment, and access to the customer dashboard.

docs.title: Billing Cycle
docs.text:
Billing is processed monthly on the anniversary of your account activation. Plan charges, surcharges, taxes, and usage-based fees appear on the same invoice.

Plan changes take effect at the start of the next billing cycle unless otherwise stated during checkout.

docs.title: Payment Methods
docs.text:
SwiftBox supports the following payment methods:

  • Credit and debit cards - Visa, Mastercard, and American Express.
  • ACH bank transfers - Available for Business and Enterprise accounts in supported regions.
  • Net-30 invoices - Available to approved Enterprise customers.

Keep at least one active payment method on file to avoid service interruption.

docs.title: Taxes
docs.text:
Listed prices do not include taxes. Applicable taxes are calculated from the billing address and shown before payment is confirmed.

  • United States - Sales tax may apply based on state and local rules.
  • European Union - VAT may apply unless a valid VAT ID is provided and accepted.

Tax rates and exemptions can change. Review each invoice for the final tax amount charged.

docs.title: Billing History
docs.text:
You can download invoices and receipts from the dashboard:

  1. Go to Billing > Invoices.
  2. Select the billing period.
  3. Choose Download PDF or Download CSV.

Invoices include the plan, shipment usage, surcharges, taxes, payment method, and billing address used for that period.

docs.title: Refund Policy
docs.text:
Monthly plans do not include refunds for unused shipments or unused time in the current billing period. Annual plans may be eligible for prorated refunds when required by contract or local law.

Shipment fees are refundable only when SwiftBox cancels the shipment before pickup or when support confirms a billing error.

docs.title: How do I upgrade my plan?
docs.text:
Navigate to Settings > Plan in your dashboard and select your desired tier. Plan changes take effect at the start of the next billing cycle unless the checkout flow states otherwise.

Note

Upgrading mid-cycle prorates the additional charges. Downgrading takes effect at the next cycle with no refunds for unused shipments.

docs.title: What payment methods are accepted?
docs.text: Starter accounts can pay by credit or debit card. Business accounts can use cards or ACH bank transfers. Enterprise customers can request ACH payments and net-30 invoice terms.

docs.title: Are there additional fees?
docs.text:
• Address corrections: $5 per correction
  • Saturday delivery: $15 surcharge
  • Signature required: $3 per shipment
  • Insurance above $100: $0.50 per $100 of coverage

Warning

Failed payments incur a $25 processing fee. SwiftBox provides a 7-day grace period to update your payment method before account suspension.

docs.title: Can I cancel my subscription?
docs.text:
Yes, you can cancel at any time from your dashboard. Service continues through the end of your current billing period with no prorated refunds for monthly plans.

Tip

Contact our sales team for volume discounts if your monthly shipping volume exceeds Enterprise tier limits.

docs.title: Getting Started with SwiftBox
docs.text: Follow these steps to create your account, configure billing, and place your first order.

docs.title: 1. Create Your Account
docs.text:
Visit swiftbox.com/signup and complete the registration form. You will need to provide:

  • Business name, if applicable
  • Contact email
  • Phone number
  • Billing address

Use an email address that your operations team can access. SwiftBox sends account verification, order confirmations, billing notices, and shipment alerts to this address.

Tip

Use a business email address if you plan to upgrade to Business or Enterprise tiers later.

docs.title: 2. Verify Your Email
docs.text:
After submitting the form, check your inbox for a verification email. Click the verification link to activate your account and unlock the SwiftBox dashboard.

If the link expires, return to the sign-in page and request a new verification email.

docs.title: 3. Complete Your Profile
docs.text:
Log in to your SwiftBox dashboard and complete your profile settings. This includes:

  • Adding saved pickup and delivery addresses
  • Setting up payment methods
  • Configuring notification preferences
  • Choosing default service levels for recurring shipments

Review these settings before creating your first order. Accurate profile details reduce address corrections, payment failures, and notification delays.

docs.title: 4. Place Your First Order
docs.text:
Navigate to New Order in the dashboard and follow these steps:

  1. Enter recipient details - Add the recipient name, address, and contact information.
  2. Specify package dimensions - Enter weight, length, width, and height.
  3. Select a service level - Choose Standard, Express, or Same-Day delivery.
  4. Choose a pickup option - Schedule pickup or drop off the shipment at a supported location.
  5. Review and confirm - Verify all details before submitting the order.

Warning

Double-check the recipient address before confirming. Address corrections after order placement may incur additional fees.

After confirmation, SwiftBox creates the order and assigns a tracking number. Save this tracking number for customer service, dashboard lookup, and API requests.

docs.title: 5. Track Your Shipment
docs.text:
Once your order is confirmed, use the tracking number to monitor the shipment in the dashboard or on the Order Tracking page. You can also retrieve tracking events through the Partner API.

Note

Your first order includes a discount. Check your email for the promo code before you confirm payment.

docs.title: Account Deletion and Data Retention
docs.text: You can request account deletion from Settings > Account or by emailing support@swiftbox.com. SwiftBox retains order, billing, and tax records as required for legal, security, and compliance purposes. Personal data that is no longer required is deleted or anonymized according to the SwiftBox retention policy.

docs.title: Did not receive the verification email?
docs.text: Check your spam or quarantine folder, confirm that the email address is correct, and request a resend from the sign-in page. If the message still does not arrive, contact support@swiftbox.com.

docs.title: Cannot add a payment method?
docs.text: Confirm that your billing address matches the payment method on file. For supported payment options by plan, see Pricing & Billing.

docs.title: Tracking number not found?
docs.text: Tracking numbers may take a few minutes to appear after order confirmation. If the status is still unavailable after 15 minutes, verify the order ID in your dashboard or contact support.

docs.title: Order Tracking
docs.text:
Monitor shipments through the SwiftBox dashboard or integrate webhook notifications for automated status updates.

Note

All timestamps in tracking responses and webhook payloads use UTC in ISO 8601 format.

docs.title: Order Status Lifecycle
docs.text:
Every shipment progresses through a standard set of statuses during delivery.

Status Description Typical Duration PENDING_PICKUP Order is confirmed and waiting for pickup scheduling or drop-off. Immediate to 1 business day PICKUP_SCHEDULED Carrier is assigned and pickup time is confirmed. 1-2 hours IN_TRANSIT Shipment is moving through the SwiftBox network. 1-5 business days OUT_FOR_DELIVERY Shipment is with the local carrier for final delivery. Same day DELIVERED Shipment was successfully delivered. Final DELIVERY_ATTEMPTED Recipient was unavailable or delivery could not be completed. 1 business day EXCEPTION Shipment is delayed due to weather, address issues, customs, or other external factors. Variable RETURNED Shipment is being returned to the sender. 1-5 business days CANCELLED Order was cancelled before delivery completion. Final

Note

Status updates may vary based on service level, destination, and external factors such as weather, holidays, or customs processing.

docs.title: Webhook Notifications
docs.text:
Configure webhooks to receive real-time status updates for your orders. Webhooks are sent as HTTP POST requests to your configured endpoint.

You can also manage webhook subscriptions with the Partner API.

docs.title: Setting Up Webhooks
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Settings > Webhooks in your dashboard.
  2. Enter your webhook URL.
  3. Select the events you want to subscribe to.
  4. Add or generate a webhook secret.
  5. Save your configuration.

docs.title: Webhook Payload Example
docs.text:
{
  "event": "order.status_updated",
  "timestamp": "2025-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "order_id": "SBX-789456123",
  "tracking_number": "1Z999AA10123456784",
  "status": "IN_TRANSIT",
  "location": {
    "city": "Chicago",
    "state": "IL",
    "country": "US"
  },
  "estimated_delivery": "2025-01-18T17:00:00Z",
  "metadata": {
    "carrier": "SwiftBox Express",
    "service_level": "standard"
  }
}

Tip

Store the raw request body before parsing JSON. Signature verification must use the exact bytes SwiftBox sent.

docs.title: Webhook Security
docs.text:
SwiftBox signs each webhook request with an HMAC-SHA256 signature in the X-SwiftBox-Signature header. Verify the signature before processing the event.

const crypto = require("crypto");

function verifySwiftBoxSignature(rawBody, signatureHeader, secret) {
  if (!signatureHeader || !secret) {
    return false;
  }

  const expectedSignature = crypto
    .createHmac("sha256", secret)
    .update(rawBody)
    .digest("hex");

  const expected = Buffer.from(expectedSignature, "hex");
  const received = Buffer.from(signatureHeader, "hex");

  return (
    expected.length === received.length &&
    crypto.timingSafeEqual(expected, received)
  );
}

Warning

Reject webhook requests that are missing a signature or fail verification. Do not process the payload until the signature is valid.

docs.title: Retry Policy
docs.text:
Your endpoint must respond with 200 OK within 5 seconds. SwiftBox retries failed deliveries with exponential backoff.

Retry Attempt Delay Before Retry Trigger 1 1 second Non-2xx response or timeout 2 2 seconds Non-2xx response or timeout 3 4 seconds Final retry after repeated failure

SwiftBox stops after 3 retry attempts. Repeated failures may disable the webhook endpoint until it is updated and re-enabled.

docs.title: Example Webhook Receiver
docs.text:
This Flask example verifies the signature, parses the event, and returns quickly. Move long-running work to a background queue.

import hashlib
import hmac
import os

from flask import Flask, abort, request

app = Flask(__name__)
WEBHOOK_SECRET = os.environ["SWIFTBOX_WEBHOOK_SECRET"]


def verify_signature(raw_body: bytes, signature: str, secret: str) -> bool:
    if not signature:
        return False

    expected = hmac.new(
        secret.encode("utf-8"),
        raw_body,
        hashlib.sha256,
    ).hexdigest()
    return hmac.compare_digest(expected, signature)


@app.post("/webhooks/swiftbox")
def receive_swiftbox_webhook():
    raw_body = request.get_data()
    signature = request.headers.get("X-SwiftBox-Signature", "")

    if not verify_signature(raw_body, signature, WEBHOOK_SECRET):
        abort(401)

    event = request.get_json(silent=True)
    if event is None:
        abort(400)

    # Store the event ID or order ID before processing to avoid duplicates.
    print(f"Received {event['event']} for order {event['order_id']}")
    return {"received": True}, 200

docs.title: Response Requirements
docs.text:
Your webhook endpoint must respond with a 200 OK status code within 5 seconds. Return a non-2xx status only when SwiftBox should retry the event.

Warning

If your webhook endpoint returns errors or times out repeatedly, notifications for that endpoint may be automatically disabled.
